name: Three-Brane and Its Throat
description: A flat sheet of three dimensions in a spacetime of ten, carrying the charge of the 5-form field of type IIB supergravity. Far from the sheet spacetime is flat, and close to it a throat of infinite length opens, anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions times a sphere of five, both of one radius. Juan Maldacena took the limit that keeps the throat alone in 1997 and conjectured that string theory there is a gauge theory in four dimensions.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\lambda{}_{\mu\lambda\nu}$.
history: String theory needs ten dimensions, and in ten dimensions a charge can sit on a sheet as easily as on a point [horowitz1991]. Gary Horowitz and Andrew Strominger went looking for the black holes of that theory and came back with "a variety of solutions with the structure of an extended object surrounded by an event horizon" [horowitz1991]. One of them is a sheet with three dimensions of space, a three-brane, which carries the charge of the 5-form field of the type IIB theory [horowitz1991]. Nine dimensions of space less the three of the sheet leave six across it, so the sphere that surrounds a three-brane has five dimensions [horowitz1991]. A sheet of three dimensions that lasts through time is a world of four, and the two of them called theirs "an interesting and concrete model for attempts to describe our universe as a threebrane embedded in a higher-dimensional spacetime" [horowitz1991].¶A black three-brane has a mass and a charge, and the charge sets a floor under the mass, as it does for a charged black hole [horowitz1991]. The three-brane that sits on that floor was written down in May 1991 by Michael Duff and Jian Xin Lu, who found that it keeps half of the theory's supersymmetry [dufflu1991]. Their line element is $$ds^2 = H^{-1/2}\left(-c^2dt^2 + dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2\right) + H^{1/2}\left(d\rho^2 + \rho^2d\Omega_5^2\right), \qquad H = 1 + \frac{L^4}{\rho^4},$$ with $\rho$ the radius in the six dimensions across the sheet and $d\Omega_5^2$ the unit sphere of five dimensions [dufflu1991]. Gravity pulls two such sheets together exactly as hard as their charges push them apart, so any number of parallel three-branes stand at rest, with one term in $H$ for each [dufflu1991, gibbons1995]. The three-brane joined the string, the fivebrane, and the membrane found since 1990, each an extended charged object at rest that keeps half the supersymmetry [dabholkar1990, callan1991, duffstelle1991, dufflu1991].¶What happens close to the sheet? Far away $H$ is 1 and spacetime is flat, but toward $\rho = 0$ the sphere stops shrinking at the radius $L$, and the distance to $\rho = 0$ along a moment of time is infinite [gibbons1993]. The three-brane is a flat plane with a pipe of infinite length let into it, and the pipe is anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions times a sphere of five, both of radius $L$ [gibbons1993]. That reading is Gary Gibbons and Paul Townsend's, who took the extreme Reissner-Nordström black hole for their model: it joins flat space of four dimensions to anti-de Sitter space of two times a sphere "down an infinite wormhole throat" [gibbons1993]. The membrane and the fivebrane of eleven dimensions have throats of their own, anti-de Sitter space of four dimensions times a sphere of seven and of seven times a sphere of four [duffstelle1991, guven1992, gibbons1993]. The three-brane shares one more property with the charged black hole: under $\rho \to L^2/\rho$ the throat and the flat region change places, with every length rescaled by $L/\rho$ [gibbons1993, couch1984].¶A horizon usually hides a singularity, and Horowitz and Strominger had put one behind the horizon of each black three-brane [horowitz1991]. Gibbons, Horowitz, and Townsend looked behind the horizon of the extreme three-brane and found none [gibbons1995]. In the coordinate $w = (1 - L^4/r^4)^{1/4}$, with $r$ the radius of the sphere, the horizon is at $w = 0$ and the metric is the same at $-w$ as at $w$, so "the spacetime behind the horizon is isometric to the region outside, and the solution is completely nonsingular" [gibbons1995]. An observer who falls through the horizon comes out in a copy of the region outside, which has a horizon of its own with another copy behind it [gibbons1995]. "The existence of solutions with horizons but no singularities is certainly surprising", the three wrote, and the singularity theorems allow it because the three-brane has no compact trapped surface [gibbons1995].¶How is the sheet itself made? Joseph Polchinski's answer of 1995 is that the charged sheets of type II string theory are D-branes, surfaces on which open strings end, and that they "carry a complete set of electric and magnetic Ramond-Ramond charges" [polchinski1995]. A three-brane with $N$ units of charge is then $N$ D-branes lying on top of one another, and the open strings between them make a gauge theory in four dimensions, $\mathcal{N} = 4$ super Yang-Mills theory with gauge group $U(N)$ [maldacena1998]. The same object now has two descriptions, a curved spacetime and a gas of open strings on a flat sheet, and the two can be checked against each other [gubser1996]. Steven Gubser, Igor Klebanov, and Amanda Peet counted the entropy of a hot three-brane both ways and found agreement "up to a mysterious factor" [gubser1996]. Klebanov then sent low energy waves at the three-brane and found the rate at which the sheet absorbs them "in exact agreement with the classical gravity" [klebanov1997].¶The last step was Juan Maldacena's, in November 1997 [maldacena1998]. He lowered the energy until the open strings on the sheets lost touch with the flat space around them, and in the spacetime the same limit keeps the throat alone: "we can neglect the 1 in the harmonic function", which leaves $$ds^2 = \frac{\rho^2}{L^2}\left(-c^2dt^2 + dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2\right) + \frac{L^2}{\rho^2}d\rho^2 + L^2d\Omega_5^2, \qquad L^4 = 4\pi gN\alpha'^2,$$ with $g$ the string coupling and $\alpha'$ the square of the string length [maldacena1998]. His conjecture is that type IIB string theory in the throat "is dual to" the gauge theory of the $N$ sheets [maldacena1998]. The rule for computing with it came in February 1998, from Gubser, Klebanov, and Alexander Polyakov and, separately, from Edward Witten: a correlation function of the gauge theory is given, in Witten's words, by "the dependence of the supergravity action on the asymptotic behavior at infinity", the edge at large $\rho$ where the flat space used to begin [gubser1998, witten1998].

related.text: The throat is anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions times a sphere, both of radius $L$. Its boundary at large $r$ is where the gauge theory of Maldacena's correspondence lives [maldacena1998, witten1998].
The same throat in four dimensions, anti-de Sitter space of two dimensions times a sphere, at the bottom of the extreme charged black hole [gibbons1993].

The charged black hole. At its largest charge it joins flat space to an infinite throat, as the three-brane does, and an inversion of the radius carries each into itself with every length rescaled [gibbons1993, couch1984].

Any number of extreme charged black holes at rest, gravity balanced by charge. Parallel three-branes stand at rest by the same balance, their $H$ a harmonic function of the six dimensions across them [dufflu1991, gibbons1995].

Schwarzschild's black hole with a flat direction added, the simplest extended black hole. Horowitz and Strominger gave such objects a charge in ten dimensions, and the three-brane is the extreme member of one of their families [horowitz1991].

The charged black hole of string theory in four dimensions. Gibbons, Horowitz, and Townsend showed that some of its extreme members are branes of more dimensions seen from four, their singularity a horizon like that of the three-brane [gibbons1995].
The black hole of anti-de Sitter space with a flat horizon. The throat of a three-brane heated a little above its least mass is that black hole in five dimensions times a sphere [maldacena1998].
The sister in eleven dimensions: anti-de Sitter space of four dimensions times a 7-sphere, the throat of a stack of membranes, with the sphere twice the radius [gibbons1993, maldacena1998].
Lin, Lunin, and Maldacena's droplets. The throat is a black disc on their plane, and small droplets spread far apart are stacks of three-branes pulled apart from each other [lin2004].
The Penrose limit of the throat along a light ray circling its 5-sphere, a plane wave of ten dimensions that keeps all 32 supersymmetries of type IIB supergravity [blau2002penrose, berenstein2002].

coordinates.name: Isotropic

parameters.description: Radius of the throat and of its sphere, a length; the brane's charge fixes it, $L^4 = 4\pi g_s N\ell_s^4$, where the integer $N$ counts the units of flux of the 5-form field through the sphere, $g_s$ is the string coupling, and $\ell_s$ is the string length
Harmonic function of the six dimensions across the brane, a pure number; it is 1 far from the brane and $L^4/\rho^4$ in the throat

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, y, z, \rho, \alpha, \beta, \psi, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ a time, $x$, $y$, and $z$ lengths along the brane, $\rho$ the isotropic radius in the six dimensions across it, and $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\psi$, $\theta$, and $\phi$ the angles on the 5-sphere. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = H^{-1/2}\left(-c^2dt^2 + dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2\right) + H^{1/2}\left(d\rho^2 + \rho^2\left(d\alpha^2 + \sin^2\alpha\left(d\beta^2 + \sin^2\beta\left(d\psi^2 + \sin^2\psi\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)
geodesics: \ddot{\rho} + \dfrac{\rho^3\,L^4}{\left(\rho^4 + L^4\right)^2}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{\rho^3\,L^4}{\left(\rho^4 + L^4\right)^2}\dot{x}^2 - \dfrac{\rho^3\,L^4}{\left(\rho^4 + L^4\right)^2}\dot{y}^2 - \dfrac{\rho^3\,L^4}{\left(\rho^4 + L^4\right)^2}\dot{z}^2 - \dfrac{L^4}{\rho\left(\rho^4 + L^4\right)}\dot{\rho}^2 - \dfrac{\rho^5}{\rho^4 + L^4}\dot{\alpha}^2 - \dfrac{\rho^5\sin^2\alpha}{\rho^4 + L^4}\dot{\beta}^2 - \dfrac{\rho^5\sin^2\alpha\sin^2\beta}{\rho^4 + L^4}\dot{\psi}^2 - \dfrac{\rho^5\sin^2\alpha\sin^2\beta\sin^2\psi}{\rho^4 + L^4}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\rho^5\sin^2\alpha\sin^2\beta\sin^2\psi\sin^2\theta}{\rho^4 + L^4}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Areal Radius

parameters.description: Radius of the throat and of its sphere, a length; the brane's charge fixes it, $L^4 = 4\pi g_s N\ell_s^4$, where the integer $N$ counts the units of flux of the 5-form field through the sphere, $g_s$ is the string coupling, and $\ell_s$ is the string length

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, y, z, r, \alpha, \beta, \psi, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ a time, $x$, $y$, and $z$ lengths along the brane, $r$ the areal radius of the 5-sphere, $r^4 = \rho^4 + L^4$ for the isotropic radius $\rho$, and $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\psi$, $\theta$, and $\phi$ the angles on the 5-sphere. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{L^4\left(r^4 - L^4\right)^{3/2}}{r^{11}}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{L^4\left(r^4 - L^4\right)^{3/2}}{r^{11}}\dot{x}^2 - \dfrac{L^4\left(r^4 - L^4\right)^{3/2}}{r^{11}}\dot{y}^2 - \dfrac{L^4\left(r^4 - L^4\right)^{3/2}}{r^{11}}\dot{z}^2 - \dfrac{4L^4}{r\left(r^4 - L^4\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r^4 - L^4\right)^2}{r^7}\dot{\alpha}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r^4 - L^4\right)^2\sin^2\alpha}{r^7}\dot{\beta}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r^4 - L^4\right)^2\sin^2\alpha\sin^2\beta}{r^7}\dot{\psi}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r^4 - L^4\right)^2\sin^2\alpha\sin^2\beta\sin^2\psi}{r^7}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r^4 - L^4\right)^2\sin^2\alpha\sin^2\beta\sin^2\psi\sin^2\theta}{r^7}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Gibbons-Horowitz-Townsend

parameters.description: Radius of the throat and of its sphere, a length; the brane's charge fixes it, $L^4 = 4\pi g_s N\ell_s^4$, where the integer $N$ counts the units of flux of the 5-form field through the sphere, $g_s$ is the string coupling, and $\ell_s$ is the string length
Areal radius of the 5-sphere, a length, with $\partial_wr = w^3r/(1 - w^4)$; it is $L$ on the horizon $w = 0$ and grows without bound as $w \to 1$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, y, z, w, \alpha, \beta, \psi, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ a time, $x$, $y$, and $z$ lengths along the brane, $w = (1 - L^4/r^4)^{1/4}$ a pure number, and $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\psi$, $\theta$, and $\phi$ the angles on the 5-sphere. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = w^2\left(-c^2dt^2 + dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2\right) + r^2\left(\dfrac{dw^2}{w^2\left(1 - w^4\right)^2} + d\alpha^2 + \sin^2\alpha\left(d\beta^2 + \sin^2\beta\left(d\psi^2 + \sin^2\psi\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)\right)\right)
geodesics: \ddot{w} + \dfrac{w^3\left(1 - w^4\right)^2}{r^2}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{w^3\left(1 - w^4\right)^2}{r^2}\dot{x}^2 - \dfrac{w^3\left(1 - w^4\right)^2}{r^2}\dot{y}^2 - \dfrac{w^3\left(1 - w^4\right)^2}{r^2}\dot{z}^2 + \dfrac{6w^4 - 1}{w\left(1 - w^4\right)}\dot{w}^2 - w^5\left(1 - w^4\right)\dot{\alpha}^2 - w^5\left(1 - w^4\right)\sin^2\alpha\,\dot{\beta}^2 - w^5\left(1 - w^4\right)\sin^2\alpha\sin^2\beta\,\dot{\psi}^2 - w^5\left(1 - w^4\right)\sin^2\alpha\sin^2\beta\sin^2\psi\,\dot{\theta}^2 - w^5\left(1 - w^4\right)\sin^2\alpha\sin^2\beta\sin^2\psi\sin^2\theta\,\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, y, z, r, \alpha, \beta, \psi, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ a time, $x$, $y$, and $z$ lengths along the brane, $r$ a length that falls to zero down the throat, and $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\psi$, $\theta$, and $\phi$ the angles on the 5-sphere. coordinates.name: Throat, Proper Distance

parameters.description: Radius of the throat and of its sphere, a length; the brane's charge fixes it, $L^4 = 4\pi g_s N\ell_s^4$, where the integer $N$ counts the units of flux of the 5-form field through the sphere, $g_s$ is the string coupling, and $\ell_s$ is the string length

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, y, z, \sigma, \alpha, \beta, \psi, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ a time, $x$, $y$, and $z$ lengths along the brane, $\sigma = L\ln(r/L)$ the proper distance along the throat for the throat's radial coordinate $r$, and $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\psi$, $\theta$, and $\phi$ the angles on the 5-sphere. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = e^{2\sigma/L}\left(-c^2dt^2 + dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2\right) + d\sigma^2 + L^2\left(d\alpha^2 + \sin^2\alpha\left(d\beta^2 + \sin^2\beta\left(d\psi^2 + \sin^2\psi\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)\right)\right)
